chief_complaint: Management of chronic anemia, prediabetes, and stage 1 hypertension during preventive health visit
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 37-year-old white male with a long-standing history of anemia diagnosed in 2010, prediabetes identified in 2009 (most recent A1c 6.1%), and stage 1 hypertension (most recent BP 136/76 mmHg). He has not had any outpatient visits since March 2021 and is not taking any medications. Socially, he reports persistent lack of transportation and transport problems, which have limited his ability to attend appointments and obtain labs. He is employed full-time and has a college education. No acute complaints are documented.
past_medical_history: Resolved gingival disease and gingivitis (treated 2021), two episodes of acute viral pharyngitis (2018, 2019), prior stress and exposure to violence in the environment (resolved 2021), and a completed medication review (2021).
social_determinants: Persistent lack of access to transportation and transport problems limit health-care access; full-time employment provides income but may constrain time; higher education may aid health literacy.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage 1 hypertension, prediabetes, chronic anemia, male sex, age 37; missing lipid panel and smoking status prevent full ASCVD calculation. Metabolic risk: prediabetes, unknown BMI, no lipid data. Hematologic risk: chronic anemia of unknown etiology. Potential renal risk due to absent eGFR and albuminuria data. Social risk: transportation barriers. Charlson comorbidity index 1; overall clinical complexity moderate.
